alignments.note: The expletive there is a supplied subject and thither realizes the preverb ἐπ- under rule 106, discontinuously under rule 15; head on the verb word.
Participle converted to a finite clause with its supplied subject.
Article before a name with no English realization; rule 23.

The expressed καί joining the two participles surfaces as the single and the ASV writes between the two English predicates; rule 88's closing clause leaves an expressed conjunction to the ordinary analysis, and rule 15 permits the placement. Leaving it unrepresented and reading t018 as a rule 88 juncture on ἔσυρον remains defensible.

σύρω expresses no object in Greek and English requires one, so the supplied him is a rule 7 helper on the verb that licenses it, exactly as the supplied of it is at 14.6 and 14.14 and them is at 14.22; rules 7, 74 and 103. Head on the lexical verb under rule 17.

αὐτόν is the accusative subject of τεθνηκέναι and is realized by the subject word of the clause the ASV expands, as αὐτούς → they at 14.1 and ἡμᾶς → we at 14.22 do. Reading him as this pronoun's own English and he as a rule 74 supplied subject on the infinitive remains defensible.
Improper preposition kept bare because the ASV writes a determiner for the governed noun, which the article takes with the case preposition; rules 42 and 101.
Article takes the determiner and carries the case preposition of; rules 21 and 101.

The infinitive is expanded into a finite clause and the supplied complementizer belongs to it under rule 85; head on the lexical predicate word. The clause's subject he belongs to the expressed αὐτόν.

review_notes: Corrected: t020 him now rides with ἔσυρον and αὐτόν keeps only t027 he. σύρω expresses no object in Greek and English requires one, so him is a rule 7 helper on the verb that licenses it (rules 7 and 103), while the expressed accusative subject of the infinitive is realized by the subject word of the clause the ASV expands, as at 14.1 and 14.22. Reading him as αὐτόν's own English and he as a rule 74 supplied subject on the infinitive remains defensible and is named in the units' notes.
ἔξω τῆς πόλεως is split as out / of the / city under rule 101, the ASV writing a determiner for the governed noun so that the article takes it and carries the case preposition.

s012 καί is aligned to the single and the ASV writes between the two English predicates; the competing reading leaves it unrepresented and reads t018 as a rule 88 juncture on ἔσυρον, and is named in that unit's note.
